newsitem.title: CHINA: Worldbest to take over plastics firm.
newsitem.headline: Worldbest to take over plastics firm.

text.p: Textile company Shanghai Worldbest Co Ltd will spend $7.65 million to take over a plastics joint venture and invest 1.9 million yuan in an investment company, a company official said on Thursday.
The plan has been approved by a meeting of the company's shareholders, the official said.
Worldbest plans to take a 51 percent stake in Changzhou Worldbest Radici Engineering Plastics Co, of which 43.5 percent is owned by Gruppo Radici S.R.I. of Italy, from China Worldbest Group, he said.

The plastics firm, in Changzhou in the eastern province of Jiangsu, produces 60,000 tonnes of polyester chips and plastic chips a year, products which Worldbest considers to have excellent market prospects, the official said.

The company will also invest 1.9 million yuan for a 38 percent stake of Shanghai Kaima International Investment Co, with China Worldbest Group taking 52 percent and China New Building Material Group Finance taking 10 percent, he said.
Separately, a Singaporean, Ke Bilang, chairman of Regional Container Lines Public, has been chosen as a director of Shanghai Worldbest, the official said but gave no more details.
